commitResults.messageTitle: Add tag and untag commands for track events
commitResults.messageBody:
Coaches need to record which track events each athlete competes in,
but tags were only a legacy field with no command to set them.

Let's add `tag INDEX t/EVENT...` and `untag INDEX t/EVENT...`:
* Events may contain letters, digits, single spaces and hyphens
  (e.g. 100m, Long Jump, 110m-Hurdles), up to 30 characters.
* Events are compared case-insensitively, so 100m and 100M are the
  same event.
* `tag` keeps existing events and reports any it skipped.
* `untag` removes nothing if any given event is missing, as that is
  likely a typo.

Shared index lookup and parsing live in EventTagCommand and
EventTagCommandParser to avoid duplicating code between the two
commands. Sample athletes now come with events, and autocomplete
suggests both commands.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

The new event tagging commands need to be described for users,
testers and developers.

Let's:
* add a UG section and command summary rows for tag and untag
* add an Event tagging section to the DG with design considerations
* add use case UC07 and manual testing steps, and mark US12 as
  implemented
* list tag and untag in the help window
* stop describing tags as a legacy field in the UG and DG

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Treat a bracketed country code as part of the phone number
commitResults.messageBody:
A bracket containing '+' (such as (+65)) now counts toward the phone number and its significant digits. Every other bracket - letters like (HP), digits like (5), or a whole number written as (91234567) - stays a note and is ignored.

AF03/#139: '(+65) 9123 4567' is accepted and its country code counts, while a number written entirely inside a note bracket is still rejected, consistent with treating bracketed digits as notes (AF02).

Expose getSignificantDigits() as the canonical comparison key (notes excluded, country code included) and route Phone equality through it, so the phone-sort (#150) and duplicate-identity (#144) fixes can share one rule. Update PhoneTest and the UG phone constraints and known issues.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep long event names readable with an ellipsis and tooltip
commitResults.messageBody:
A legacy event name longer than the current limit was clipped off the athlete card in a small window, with no way to read it. A long name is now shortened with an ellipsis to fit the card, and an instant tooltip - attached only while the name is actually truncated - reveals the full value on hover. The stored value is unchanged.

AF08 / #141. Removes the matching UG known-issue entry.

commitResults.messageTitle: Order event chips ignoring case to match command feedback
commitResults.messageBody: Event chips on the athlete card sorted case-sensitively, so events such as alpha and Zulu appeared in a different order than tag/untag command feedback, which sorts ignoring case. The card now uses the same case-insensitive order (EventTagCommand's rule).

The UI section carried two conflicting descriptions of how the window remembers its bounds: an older reachability-check version and the current WindowPlacement.fit version. Removed the stale paragraph so one accurate description remains (fit onto a connected screen; normal bounds survive maximize/minimize/full-screen; written to preferences on shutdown).

Closes #139

Treat a bracketed country code as part of the phone number

commitResults.messageTitle: Guide the user when the athlete list is empty
commitResults.messageBody:
The roster area was blank with no guidance when the roster was empty (first launch or after clear). It now shows a context-aware placeholder: how to add an athlete when the roster itself is empty, or a 'no matching athletes, run list' note when a find or filter matched nothing - two states the app previously could not tell apart.

Exposes Logic#getRoster() so the UI can distinguish an empty roster from an empty filtered view. AF21 / #147.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the displayed count as X of Y when a filter or find hides athletes
commitResults.messageBody: After a find or filter, the next command replaced the feedback message and nothing showed a selection was still active; the status bar only reported the displayed count with no total. It now shows 'X of Y athletes' while some athletes are hidden, so an active filter or find stays visible even after a later sort, and 'Y athletes' when the whole roster is displayed. AF19 / #146.

Resolved the UserGuide known-issues conflict: kept master's updated phone-notes entry, and dropped both the 'pasted whitespace' entry (fixed on master) and the 'long stored event names' entry (fixed by AF08 on this branch).

Previously-valid formatting, including notes and country codes written
directly against the digits, still passes.
